title: Étale prime-power quotient map into an adapted admissible subalgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $q\subset\Lambda$ a prime, $n\ge1$, $L=\Lambda_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $J=qL$, $B=L/J^n$, and $\pi:L\to B$ the quotient map. Let $A\subset B$ be a local $k$-subalgebra with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, admissible [def-weil-pbc-popescu-admissible-subalgebra] for $JB$, and assume $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap JB$. Fix $m\ge0$ and $\varphi:k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], put $p=\varphi^{-1}(q)$ and $P=k[y]_p$, and fix a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] ring map $\psi:P\to L$ extending $\Lambda\to L$ composed with $\varphi$. Assume $qL=pL$. Suppose $a_j\in A$ map to $\pi(\varphi(y_j))$ and their residue differentials span $\Omega_{F/k}$ over $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then there is a ring map $f:P/(pP)^n\to A$ sending the maximal ideal into $\mathfrak m_A$, étale (finitely presented, formally smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], with zero relative Kähler differentials), whose composite with $A\hookrightarrow B$ and $P\to P/(pP)^n$ equals $\pi\circ\psi$. No coordinates are chosen, and neither characteristic nor geometric regularity is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: The polynomial evaluation factors through $A$ because its variable and coefficient images lie in $A$. Elements outside $p$ map outside $JB$, hence outside $\mathfrak m_A$ by contraction, hence to units of $A$. Extend to $P\to A$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Its composite with inclusion equals $\pi\psi$ by localization uniqueness. Since $qL=pL$, this composite kills $(pP)^n$. Inclusion is injective, so quotient universality gives $f:P/(pP)^n\to A$ and its compatibility equation. It is local because $p$ maps into the contracted maximal ideal.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: The map $P/(pP)^n\to B$ is the base change of $\psi$ since $pL=qL$, so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. The admissible inclusion $A\to B$ is flat and local, hence faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-permanence] to obtain flatness of $f$.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: The extensions to $B$ of $pA$ and $\mathfrak m_A$ both equal $JB$: for the former use $pL=qL$, and for the latter use admissibility. Faithfully flat contraction [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] gives $pA=\mathfrak m_A$. This is also the image of the maximal ideal of $P/(pP)^n$; the base and target are Artinian local [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] and admissibility.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: The residue field $F$ of $A$ is finitely generated over $k$, since $A$ is essentially of finite type, and hence over $\kappa(p)$. The surjection $\Omega_{F/k}\to\Omega_{F/\kappa(p)}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] kills the differentials of all coordinate residues. These span by hypothesis, so $\Omega_{F/\kappa(p)}=0$. The extension is finite separable by [lem-weil-pbc-fg-field-zero-differentials-separable].

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: The Artinian ring $A$ has residue field finite over $P/(pP)^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-finite-over-residue-finite], it is finite over that base, hence finite type. The base is Noetherian (polynomial localization followed by quotient), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] gives finite presentation.

source.place: Proof of Tag 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo); read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FH

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-flat-unramified-etale] to the finitely presented flat local map $f$, using $pA=\mathfrak m_A$ and the finite separable residue field extension. This gives algebraic étaleness at the unique prime of the Artinian local target, hence everywhere; no comparison to an affine scheme is needed.
